long_biography.plain_text:
Raised in Vigan in a politically connected and commercially active family, Luis “Chavit” Crisologo Singson began selling peanuts in his parents’ cinema before moving into tobacco trading. Tobacco became his first major business engine, after which he built interests in transport and other industries. He later consolidated a broader portfolio under the LCS Group of Companies.

Singson pursued business and public office in parallel. He served repeated terms as governor of Ilocos Sur, represented the province in Congress and later became mayor of Narvacan. His group expanded across property development, mining, renewable power, aviation, automotive distribution and telecommunications. That diversification, rather than public office or any single later investment, defines his present commercial identity.

Singson built the tobacco and later operating businesses, but he also acknowledged financially comfortable parents and began working within their cinema. Singson's elected and appointed offices are a defining public identity but are not treated as an industry or source of private wealth. The dossier classifies only the documented private operating businesses and keeps public assets, provincial revenues and official authority separate.
